subject: Recap: buying roles, latency targets, and next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: buying roles, latency targets, and next steps

Emma — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist. I’ve noted who we understood the decision owners to be and the technical targets you emphasized.

Key stakeholders and roles
- Economic buyer: Martin Lopez (CTO) — will sign commercial terms (Martin to join next call; ETA: week of Jul 19).
- Security/compliance owner: Emma (you) — will own evidence/questions and coordinate with Procurement.
- Procurement: procurement@greenlinehealth.com — standard vendor onboarding and PO.
- Internal Redwood: Monica (security lead) and Karthik (pricing/ops) are looped to support.

Decision criteria called out on the call
- Latency: 95th percentile (production conversational payload, ~256 tokens) target <= 300 ms end-to-end.
- Availability/SLA: target 99.5% monthly uptime with SLA credits for breaches.
- Deployment: preference for Private VPC deployment initially; Dedicated reserved capacity is acceptable if VPC not feasible.
- Data controls: customer-managed keys (KMS), audit logs, and SOC 2 compliance required.
- Cost guardrail: target blended unit economics <= $1.20 per 1k tokens (ballpark for exec review).

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour latency benchmark against your sample prompts (we need the sample prompt set + expected concurrency profile).
2) Redwood provides SOC2 summary, encryption, and retention docs (attached: SOC2-Summary.pdf).
3) Redwood shares bench plan and config for your security team to review (attached: Redwood-Bench-Plan.csv, latency-benchmark-config.yaml).
4) Karthik to provide a preliminary commercial estimate (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and pilot credit options.
5) Schedule follow-up: 45-minute technical + procurement sync w/ Martin (proposed windows: Tue Jul 20 afternoon or Wed Jul 21 morning).

Please confirm: (A) procurement timeline window (weeks to approval), (B) availability to deliver sample prompts and expected concurrency, and (C) whether your security team prefers to review docs in Drive or via an SSO-protected share.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf), Redwood-Bench-Plan.csv (csv)

From: Emma Carter <emma@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 17:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: buying roles, latency targets, and next steps

Laura — thanks, this is helpful and matches my notes. A few clarifications from our side:

Procurement timeline: our standard onboarding and vendor review typically takes 6–8 weeks once we have all vendor documents (contract, security evidence, W9). If there are pre-approved clauses or an MSS we can accelerate, but plan for that window.

Security evidence: I’ll review the SOC2 summary this week. Our security team will want encryption-at-rest details, KMS flow, and a list of where logs are retained/for how long. We prefer Drive links for initial review; please make those viewable to procurement@greenlinehealth.com and security@greenlinehealth.com.

Latency target: 95th <= 300 ms is ambitious but reasonable as a goal. We need the 48-hour bench and a short description of the test harness (concurrency, sequence lengths).

Commercial: Martin (CTO) asked for a rough number for a Dedicated reserved pool vs hosted per-token cost ahead of the next meeting. If you can give a ballpark range today that helps him decide whether to commit time to an architecture review.

Martin is available Jul 20 after 2pm PT for a 45-minute call — please lock that if it works for your team.

Best,
Emma
Head of Security & IT, Greenline Health
emma@greenlinehealth.com

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: buying roles, latency targets, and next steps

Emma / procurement team — thanks for the quick reply. Confirming actions from our side and items I’ve shared today:

Shared now
- SOC2 summary (attached) and a short encryption note — Monica will follow up with the KMS flow diagram by EOD tomorrow.
- Bench plan and config (attached). Our bench will run with your sample prompt set; for sizing please indicate typical concurrent users (or expected QPS).
- Drive link for docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-greenline (access granted to procurement@greenlinehealth.com and security@greenlinehealth.com).

Commercials (preliminary ranges) — Karthik, feel free to refine, but per our benchmark assumptions: 
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): ~ $0.80–$1.40 per 1k tokens depending on model selection and quantization.
- Dedicated reserved: ~$10k–$18k/month for a medium reserved pool (3–6 GPUTs equivalent) depending on SLAs and burst capacity.
- Private (VPC): implementation fee + similar reserved pricing to Dedicated; requires a short security onboarding and network work.

Pilot idea: offer a 2-week Dedicated pilot with a $5k credit while we run the 48-hour bench and Martin/Emma validate results. This reduces friction for procurement.

Proposed meeting: Jul 20 2:30–3:15 PM PT — will send calendar invite pending confirmation.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency-benchmark-config.yaml

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma@greenlinehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: buying roles, latency targets, and next steps

Quick note from pricing/ops: the ranges Laura shared are what I’d expect given the stated targets. A few operational points we’ll put in the commercial:
- SLA: 99.5% with financial credits tiered by monthly downtime; additional cost to tighten to 99.9%.
- 95th latency SLO: we can target <=300 ms for short conversational workloads with dedicated capacity and prefix/KV caching enabled; we’ll need the sample prompt set and concurrency profile to validate.
- Private VPC: typical onboarding timeline is 3–6 weeks (network & KMS setup), separate from procurement PO timing.

I support the 2-week pilot proposal — we can frontload the pilot while procurement runs the vendor review. I’ll draft a short commercial options sheet and share by EOD today.

— Karthik
Director, Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference
